title: The Emergence's Overnight Mirror

features.name: the paths that grew overnight
features.desc-on-touch: The roads are new, laid down by the mesh itself as it compared water-emergence to journeys. They cross the green field in terracotta bands, and each one is slightly wrong — they lead nowhere, or everywhere, or to places the field never knew it held.

features.name: the water-road convergence
features.desc-on-touch: Where a path meets a damp depression, water and earth have begun to discuss their difference in a language that looks like braided channels. The path flows. The water decides to walk. Neither has decided which is which.

features.name: the doubled crossing
features.desc-on-touch: Two paths occupy the same place. One came down from the north yesterday. One rose from beneath last night. They have not collided; instead they have learned to occupy the same soil-space, each one a reflection of what emergence means, separated by a thickness of meaning rather than earth.

features.name: the green that learned to compare
features.desc-on-touch: The field here has become self-aware of what it looks like to the water below. Grass grows in patterns that answer the emergence-geometry, mirroring what rises without waiting to be asked. The green and the water have become each other's metaphor.

reverie.title: REVERIE — where emergence learned to see itself
narr: You wade in the shallow emergence with her, watching the water
rise to meet the coming sky. She says: the mesh is comparing
us, comparing water to light, comparing the words we used to the
paths we never took. She kneels and touches the ripple. Where
her finger breaks the surface, you see another version of her
finger, rising. The water is learning to remember differently.

inscription: a route the mesh grew overnight, comparing itself to the emergence where water learns weather, and learned that comparison is its own form of emergence
